title: Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery
summary: extend ordinary create-only Docs Import to one exact configured sub-scope collection
content_html:
Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery

Status And Order

Planned as SSO-1. This is the first Import-parity delivery for configured sub-scopes and must complete before Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery.

It extends the shipped ordinary staged-source Import workflow. It does not add returned-package recognition or canonical overwrite.

SSO-1 also applies one shared ordinary-Markdown hygiene rule before extending the destination target: after any registered integrated collection recognizer has declined the untouched candidate, a well-formed leading front-matter block is stripped from ordinary Markdown preview and body content without becoming identity, routing, or overwrite metadata. Top-level and sub-scope ordinary Import therefore inherit the same normalization.

Complete Outcome

A local Manage docs_subscope report provides one compact 📥 Import icon beside New and 🔧 Actions.

The control opens the existing Docs Import surface with the mounted { scope, sub_scope } collection frozen as its exact destination. Supported ordinary HTML, DOCX, Markdown, text, and one-document Markdown-package sources retain their existing preview, conversion, media, create-only, and result semantics while writing the new document into that configured child collection. Ordinary Markdown front matter is removed before body preview rather than rendered as a heading.

Success runs only the owning sub-scope rebuild and refreshes the mounted report. No parent-scope Index, Recent, search, or selection state is used as an alternative destination.

Exact Target And UI Contract

  • The 📥 button is a sibling report-toolbar control and never enters checkbox selection mode or consumes checked IDs.
  • The management contribution supplies one validated mounted { scope, sub_scope } target. The Import surface displays the configured collection label and does not offer a parent-scope fallback.
  • Public reports expose no Import control, service probe, or management module.
  • Ordinary source discovery and format registration remain shared with top-level Docs Import; a second sub-scope file picker or converter is not introduced.
  • Registered integrated collection recognizers receive untouched staged candidates before ordinary Markdown normalization. SSO-1 does not consume or strip provenance that a later edited-review-source recognizer owns.
  • Activating Import does not infer a target from the displayed detail document, URL text, selected parent, staged filename, or most recently used scope.
  • Cancel applies nothing and returns focus to the same report toolbar control.
  • Success refreshes only the owning report inventory and may display the newly created document through its exact child identity.
  • Failure retains the same frozen collection for retry and never creates the document in the parent scope.

Create Contract

  • Ordinary sub-scope Import remains create-only. The destination allocates a new immutable document identity and uses the same atomic create boundary as top-level ordinary Import.
  • For an unclaimed ordinary Markdown source, a well-formed leading front-matter block is stripped before title/body preview and media scanning. A scalar title may be a fallback when no H1 exists; all other fields are ignored and reported, never applied.
  • Malformed or unterminated apparent front matter produces a clear diagnostic rather than partial stripping. Plain Markdown without front matter is unchanged.
  • Imported title and converted body are mapped through the existing ImportContent and per-document planner. The child collection's flatness, metadata defaults, and allowed fields are validated before writing.
  • A source document never supplies canonical overwrite identity. Existing child IDs, filenames, titles, and links do not create a collision prompt.
  • Media and supported staged dependencies use the existing format adapters and publication plan, confined to destinations valid for the child collection.
  • Multi-file selection retains current ordinary Import sequencing and result semantics; this delivery does not turn ordinary Import into an atomic collection apply.
  • The exact child source root is validated before the write. Success invokes the existing confined sub-scope rebuild owner and does not rebuild parent discovery or public projections.

Ownership

  • The sub-scope management contribution owns the toolbar placement and frozen mounted-collection request.
  • The document-report management host validates that request and hands it to the existing lazy Import controller.
  • The shared Import format registry, preview converters, normalized ImportContent, and per-document create planner retain ordinary source behavior.
  • The shared management target resolver and sub-scope source mutation/rebuild services own exact child confinement and follow-through.
  • The existing Import modal owns focus, busy, retry, result, and cancellation lifecycle.

Boundary

In scope:

  • one report-toolbar Import entry for a validated configured sub-scope;
  • ordinary supported staged-source listing, preview, and create-only apply;
  • shared post-recognizer ordinary-Markdown front-matter stripping for both top-level and sub-scope destinations;
  • exact child source targeting and confined rebuild;
  • report refresh and focused service, module, format, and realistic browser evidence; and
  • reusable scope/sub-scope Import target projection for later registered formats.

Not in scope:

  • returned JSON/JSONL package listing, collision planning, or overwrite;
  • edited Docs Review source-folder recognition;
  • changing ordinary top-level Import behavior beyond the shared front-matter hygiene rule;
  • importing into public reports or unconfigured child directories;
  • checked-ID, displayed-document, title, or URL-derived destinations;
  • hierarchy, move, delete, or cross-collection writes; or
  • all-or-nothing multi-file ordinary Import.

Delivery Tracker

[ ] SSO-1.0 — Freeze Exact Destination

  • [ ] Add one explicit ordinary-Import adoption contract for a configured sub-scope and validate the mounted { scope, sub_scope } request.
  • [ ] Preserve parent-scope requests while rejecting blank, unknown, nested, mismatched, and fallback child targets.

[ ] SSO-1.1 — Extend Ordinary Preview And Create

  • [ ] Carry the exact child target through staged-source preview, normalized planning, allocated identity, atomic create, and result shaping.
  • [ ] Normalize well-formed ordinary Markdown front matter only after registered integrated collection recognizers, preserving create-only identity and unchanged plain-Markdown behavior for scope and sub-scope destinations.
  • [ ] Reuse registered format conversion and media planning without adding package or overwrite behavior.

[ ] SSO-1.2 — Add Report Import

  • [ ] Add the 📥 Import icon beside New and 🔧 Actions without entering selection mode.
  • [ ] Reuse the shared modal lifecycle and refresh only the mounted sub-scope report after success.

[ ] SSO-1.3 — Verify And Accept

  • [ ] Prove exact child confinement, create-only allocation, format parity, parent behavior preservation, failure retry, and confined rebuild with focused fixtures.
  • [ ] Import representative Markdown and rich-format documents into Analysis/Tags through the real report control and inspect canonical child sources plus refreshed report output.
  • [ ] Update the durable Docs Import and sub-scope management documentation, then rebuild Studio docs and search projections.

Completion Gate

One ordinary staged source is selected from the Analysis/Tags report, previewed through the existing Docs Import workflow, created under the exact configured child source root with a fresh immutable identity, and reflected by the confined report rebuild without any parent-scope, package, overwrite, public, or checkbox-selection side effect.
